text:
A regional bank's marketing team wants to demonstrate to clients how the dollar gap between continuous compounding and ordinary annual compounding changes with the interest rate and the holding period. It compares nominal rates of 3% and 15%, each applied for 1 year to a \$25,000 deposit, and then extends the 3% case to an 8-year horizon.

**Part 1: Setup.**

Record the given quantity:

$$P = 25,000$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$25,000.

The two nominal annual rates are $r = 3\%$ and $r = 15\%$.

The account compounds continuously. vs. annual (m = 1)

The main time horizon is $t = 1$ years (and 8 years for part d, e).

**Part 2: Formula.**

Use the following relationship:

$$S_{\mathrm{cont}} = P \times e^{rt}$$

Use the following relationship:

$$S_{\mathrm{annual}} = P \times (1+r)^{t}$$

**Part 3: Solve.**

**1.** At $3\%$, $1$ yr: the value computed below.

$$S_{\mathrm{cont}} = 25,000 \times e^{0.03}$$

$$= 25,761.36$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$25,761.36.

**2.** Substitute the stated values:

$$S_{\mathrm{annual}} = 25,000 \times 1.03$$

$$= 25,750.00$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$25,750.00.

**3.** Gap: the value computed below.

$$11.36$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$11.36.

**4.** At $15\%$, $1$ yr: the value computed below.

$$S_{\mathrm{cont}} = 25,000 \times e^{0.15}$$

$$= 29,045.86$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$29,045.86.

**5.** Substitute the stated values:

$$S_{\mathrm{annual}} = 25,000 \times 1.15$$

$$= 28,750.00$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$28,750.00.

**6.** Gap: the value computed below.

$$295.86$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$295.86.

**7.** Ratio: the value computed below, which is less than $30$.

$$295.86 / 11.36 \approx 26.04$$

**8.** At $3\%$, $8$ yrs: the value computed below.

$$S_{\mathrm{cont}} = 25,000 \times e^{0.24}$$

$$= 31,781.23$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$31,781.23.

**9.** Substitute the stated values:

$$S_{\mathrm{annual}}(8) = 25,000 \times (1.03)^{8}$$

$$= 25,000 \times 1.266770$$

$$= 31,669.25$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$31,669.25.

**10.** Compute the stated difference:

$$31,781.23 - 31,669.25 = 111.98$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$111.98.

text:
An investment advisory firm is evaluating a \$400,000 allocation and comparing two funds that both quote a nominal annual rate of 9.5%: Fund A compounds continuously, while Fund B compounds monthly. The firm also wants to check whether switching Fund B to daily compounding could ever let it catch up to or overtake Fund A.

**Part 1: Setup.**

Record the given quantity:

$$P = 400,000$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$400,000.

Nominal annual rate r = i = 9.5% = 0.095

Fund A compounds continuously.

Fund B compounds monthly with $m = 12$; the later comparison uses daily compounding with $m = 365$.

The main time horizon is $t = 1$ years.

**Part 2: Formula.**

Use the following relationship:

$$S_A = P \times e^{rt}$$

Use the following relationship:

$$S_B = P \times (1+i/m)^{mt}$$

Use the following relationship:

$$EAR_{\mathrm{max}} = e^{r} - 1$$

**Part 3: Solve.**

**1.** Fund A: the value computed below.

$$S_A = 400,000 \times e^{0.095}$$

$$= 400,000 \times 1.0996589$$

$$= 439,863.54$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$439,863.54.

**2.** Fund B (monthly) periodic rate: $0.095/12 = 0.0079167$.

**3.** Substitute the stated values:

$$S_B = 400,000 \times (1.0079167)^{12}$$

$$= 400,000 \times 1.0992476$$

$$= 439,699.03$$

$$439,750.00$$

The corresponding monetary figures are \$439,699.03, and \$439,750.00.

**4.** the value computed below, which exceeds the $9.50\%$ nominal rate; it is not equal to it.

$$EAR_{\mathrm{max}} = e^{0.095} - 1 \approx 9.97\%$$

**5.** Fund B (daily): the value computed below, which is still below the value computed below.

$$S_{\mathrm{daily}} = 400,000 \times (1 + 0.095/365)^{365}$$

$$= 400,000 \times 1.0996453$$

$$= 439,858.10$$

$$S_A = 439,863.54$$

The corresponding monetary figures are \$439,858.10, and \$439,863.54.

**6.** Gap (continuous vs monthly): the value computed below.

$$439,863.54 - 439,699.03 = 164.51$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$164.51.

**7.** Gap (continuous vs daily): the value computed below, which is narrower than the monthly gap of the value computed below.

$$439,863.54 - 439,858.10 = 5.44$$

$$164.51$$

The corresponding monetary figures are \$5.44, and \$164.51.

Record the given quantity:

$$S_0 = 28,000$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$28,000.

The corresponding monetary figure is \$34,200.

The account compounds continuously.

The main time horizon is $t = 3$ years (observed); project to t = 5 years.

**Part 2: Formula.**

$$S(t) = S_0 e^{rt} \Rightarrow r$$

$$= \ln(S(t)/S_0)/t$$

Doubling time: the value computed below

$$39,078.52$$

**5.** Doubling time: the value computed below years.

$$\ln(2)/0.066674 = 0.693147/0.066674 \approx 10.3961$$

**6.** At $r = 6.00\%$: the value computed below, which is LOWER than the actual observed the value computed below, not higher.

$$S(3) = 28,000 \times e^{0.18}$$

$$= 28,000 \times 1.197217$$

$$= 33,522.09$$

$$34,200.00$$

text:
A municipal finance office is comparing four compounding schedules, all at the same nominal annual rate of 7%, applied to a \$40,000 reserve fund for exactly 1 year: annual, quarterly, monthly, and continuous. The office wants to confirm the textbook's claim that increasing compounding frequency strictly increases the year-end value, up to the continuous-compounding ceiling.

**Part 1: Setup.**

Record the given quantity:

$$P = 40,000$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$40,000.

Nominal annual rate i = r = 7% = 0.07

The schedules are annual with $m = 1$, quarterly with $m = 4$, monthly with $m = 12$, and continuous.

The main time horizon is $t = 1$ years.

**Part 2: Formula.**

Use the following relationship:

$$S_m = P(1+i/m)^{m}$$

$$m$$

Use the following relationship:

$$S_{\mathrm{cont}} = P e^{r}$$

**Part 3: Solve.**

**1.** Annual: the value computed below.

$$S = 40,000 \times 1.07$$

$$= 42,800.00$$

The corresponding monetary figure is \$42,800.00.

**2.** Quarterly: the value computed below.

$$S = 40,000 \times (1.0175)^{4}$$

$$= 40,000 \times 1.0718590$$

$$= 42,874.36$$

**3.** Monthly: the value computed below.

$$S = 40,000 \times (1.0058333)^{12}$$

$$= 40,000 \times 1.0722901$$

$$= 42,891.60$$

**4.** Continuous: the value computed below.

$$S = 40,000 \times e^{0.07}$$

$$42,891.60 - 42,874.36 = 17.24$$
